rationale: Tests recall of the canonical 1948 WHO definition of health, the most frequently examined fact from this block.
Tests direct recall of Winslow's (1920) definition of public health, a standard exam fact.
Tests understanding of Leavell and Clark's levels of prevention — specifically which level maps to the prepathogenesis period.
Tests understanding of the three components of the epidemiological triad and their interplay.
Tests recall of the Ottawa Charter (1986) definition of health promotion, a key fact from this block.
Tests understanding of the distinction between IEC and BCC — a common point of confusion examined in CM.
Tests recall of the correct denominator for the Maternal Mortality Ratio — a commonly confused indicator on exams.
Tests understanding of India's demographic dividend concept and the age-dependency ratio from the demographic profile block.
Tests understanding of the documented link between non-adherence and poor communication, grounded in the burden block.
Tests understanding of the Calgary-Cambridge framework as a structured consultation model, from the active listening block.
